watchedProperties.buildingHistory: Architects Joseph Krakower and Herb Greene designed this building for the Southwestern Bell Telephone Company, and it opened in 1959. The design reflects the “American School” of architecture, a design movement that Greene helped to originate in the late 1950s. This was intended to be a modern, distinctly American building without clear references to historic architecture. The building was originally painted a uniform off-white color with some accents of turquoise mosaic tile, which are mostly painted over but still present. The building got an early version of its current two-tone paint scheme from a later tenant, the Uniroyal Tire Company, which painted the upper section black to resemble a tire tread - a clever adaptation of Greene’s detailing.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search simplified street address, owner, and buyer names for published legal notices.
checklist.typicalTiming: Any stage.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Drive by and photograph the site. Look for TABC 60-day signs, plat or variance signs, fencing, dumpsters, and survey stakes.
checklist.typicalTiming: Any stage. Posted signs can appear before records show up online.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search Block & Subdivision keywords or Grantor/Grantee names for deeds, deeds of trust (naming the lender), and purchase options.
checklist.typicalTiming: Deeds usually record within days of closing.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Look up each LLC across TX Comptroller Active Sales Taxpayer Search, Franchise Tax Account Status, Bizapedia, and TX SOSDirect to find officers, registered agents, and related entities.
checklist.typicalTiming: As soon as a new entity name surfaces.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search the 13-digit HCAD account number to confirm the owner of record, legal description, and land/improvement value shifts.
checklist.typicalTiming: Owner updates lag the deed by weeks to months.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search simplified primary and perimeter addresses for pending or active TABC permits revealing operator LLCs and trade names.
checklist.typicalTiming: Often filed months before construction or demolition permits.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search DSHS Consumable Hemp registrations by entity name, DBA/trade name, or officer name (portal does not search by street address).
checklist.typicalTiming: After closing or lease execution for convenience-store operators.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search Houston Sold Permits by simplified primary and perimeter addresses for building, plumbing/water-wastewater, sewer disconnect, and demolition permits (reveals 8-digit project numbers needed for ILMS below).
checklist.typicalTiming: Any stage from early plumbing/remodel permits through final demolition permits (also provides 8-digit project numbers for ILMS).

checklist.whatToLookFor: Look up 8-digit project numbers (found via Sold Permits above) in COH ILMS, or submit a GovQA open records request covering all perimeter block addresses.
checklist.typicalTiming: Design and plan-review phase after closing.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Check Biweekly Planning Commission spreadsheets, Agenda Outlines (Section K DPV), and Public Hearing Notices for replats or variances.
checklist.typicalTiming: Can be filed before closing with seller consent or during design.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search simplified primary and perimeter addresses, DBAs, and owner LLCs in TDLR TABS (required for commercial projects >= $50,000).
checklist.typicalTiming: Design phase, often months before building or demolition permits.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Check City Council NovusAgenda packets for street, alley, or easement abandonments and check local TIRZ board agendas.
checklist.typicalTiming: Design phase, usually after closing.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Search TCEQ Central Registry for underground petroleum storage tanks (PST) or construction stormwater registrations.
checklist.typicalTiming: Shortly before construction, especially for fuel canopies and larger commercial sites.

checklist.whatToLookFor: Check Houston 311 complaints and cross-check periodic City Dangerous Buildings (DONDB) CSV lists so historic buildings can be flagged.
checklist.typicalTiming: Any stage, especially while a structure is vacant.

checklist.whatToLookFor: DSHS must be notified at least 10 working days before any commercial or public building is abated or demolished.
checklist.typicalTiming: At least 10 working days before abatement or demolition starts.
